questions.stem: What are the three fundamental types of data?
questions.explanation: In data management the three fundamental types are structured, semi-structured and unstructured data.

options: Organised in a predefined format, typically rows and columns
Data that changes structure on every entry
questions.explanation: Structured data has a stable, predefined format known before data entry, which makes extraction easy and automated.

questions.stem: A table with 6 columns and 10 rows is exported. Some cells are empty. What type of data is it?
options: The structure stays intact: every row keeps the same number of columns
Columns with empty cells are removed
It must be converted to JSON
questions.explanation: Structured data keeps its format regardless of missing entries — 6 columns and 10 rows remain.

questions.stem: Which formats are examples of semi-structured data?
questions.explanation: XML and JSON allow flexibility in structure, so they are often categorised as semi-structured.

questions.stem: How does semi-structured data differ from structured data when exported, in the employee-contact example?
options: Rows may have varying numbers of columns because only populated fields are included
It cannot be exported at all
Every row has exactly six columns
questions.explanation: Semi-structured data does not keep a consistent set of fields across entries; empty fields may be omitted, so column counts vary.

questions.stem: Which platforms are examples of sources of semi-structured data?
questions.explanation: User-generated content on platforms like Facebook or Twitter varies widely in format.

questions.stem: Which of these is typical UNSTRUCTURED data?
options: Images, videos, audio files, emails and PDFs
A JSON document with fixed keys
questions.explanation: Unstructured data lacks a predefined structure — images, videos, audio, emails, documents, presentations and PDFs.

questions.stem: What can sometimes impose a semblance of structure on unstructured data?
questions.explanation: Metadata can help impose a semblance of structure on unstructured data such as an image library.

questions.stem: Which is a characteristic of unstructured data?
options: Format unknown until examined, with continuous analysis required
questions.explanation: Unstructured data's format is unknown until examined; it needs ongoing assumptions and continuous analysis, and machine learning can find insights in it.

questions.stem: In the facial-image illustration, what makes it possible for algorithms to extract features consistently?
options: Aligning all images consistently in a structured grid, helped by metadata
Reducing every image to one pixel
questions.explanation: If all images are aligned in a structured grid and metadata ensures consistency, coded algorithms can extract the facial features.
